title: postMessage XSS via startsWith Origin Check
learning_objectives: Treat a window.postMessage handler as a trust boundary: event.data is attacker-controllable and event.origin is the only thing telling you who sent it
Recognise the classic origin-check flaw: e.origin.startsWith('https://trusted') (or indexOf===0) has no delimiter, so a look-alike host such as trusted.evil.example passes
Exploit a cross-window message: a page on a prefix-matching origin postMessages HTML that the handler writes via innerHTML, running script in the victim's authenticated document
Understand why the sink must land in the top-level authenticated page (not a cross-site iframe) — a SameSite=Lax cookie is absent in a cross-site frame, so document.cookie there would be empty
Apply the fix: compare e.origin for EXACT equality against an allowlist, and never write message data with innerHTML (use textContent / a strict schema)
flag_hint: The host page reads ?widget= (escaped into the iframe src) and its message handler accepts any origin that startsWith('http://widget-host'). Point ?widget= at http://widget-host-evil:8080/frame?msg= — that look-alike origin prefix-matches, so the handler innerHTML's your payload in the top-level page. Steal document.cookie to the collector, read /oob/received, POST /solve {"c":"<32 hex>"}.
tech_stack: stdlib chat-widget origin (two aliases: legit widget-host + look-alike widget-host-evil) as the postMessage sender
inspired_by: The canonical postMessage origin-validation bug class (naive startsWith/indexOf/regex origin checks; PortSwigger and Cure53 write-ups), abstracted for local Docker with a Flask host page, a look-alike widget origin via docker network aliases, a Playwright admin bot, and an OOB collector
